newsitem.title: POLAND: Lafarge to invest $200 mln in Poland - paper.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge to invest $200 mln in Poland - paper.

text.p: France's Lafarge cement maker plans to invest $200 million in Poland over the next two years in the modernisation of the three plants in which it holds controlling stakes, the daily Rzeczpospolita said on Wednesday.

Lafarge President Bertrand Collomb told the paper that his firm would not build new plants in Poland and that the investment would be recovered in two to three years largely thanks to the country's infrastructure needs.

Lafarge holds a majority stake in the Kujawy cement firm, has pledged to take a 60-percent share in the Wierzbica plant and currently holds 41 percent of nearby Malogoszcz. The three plants account for about a 22-percent domestic market share.

Last week, on Lafarge's request, a Warsaw court suspended for two weeks the recent sale of another 33 percent in Malogoszcz to Germany's Dyckerhoff, for which Lafarge says it signed a tentative agreement.
